comment: Acceptance matrix for the black-box template. Unlike white-box, nothing here is checked against fixed
expectations - the competitor's suite is measured, so the assertions are quality bands.
The row that matters is 'weak': it has the same line coverage as the reference suite but asserts nothing
meaningful, so it must score clearly lower. If it ever scores close to 'reference', the mutation ramp in
marking-map.json has stopped doing any work and the constants need retuning.
Observed at the time of writing, with coverage 30..95 and mutation 20..90:
reference  coverage 1.00  kill 0.83  quality 0.97
weak       coverage 1.00  kill 0.33  quality 0.61
empty      coverage 0     kill 0     quality 0
The reference sits above the 0.8-0.9 headroom a real session should aim for; this fixture is a six-mutant
toy, so it is not worth over-tuning. Calibrate per session against the real reference suite.

personas.name: reference
comment: The suite the module ships with. The calibration target.
Split across two test classes - CalculatorTests and DescribeTests - so the per-fixture assertions
have something to distinguish. With one class they would be satisfied by a judge that measured the
whole suite once and labelled the result with the only fixture name it could see.
coverageTotal/coverageCovered are the only exact numbers in this file. Calculator.cs has three
coverable lines and the reference suite reaches all three, and unlike a kill rate that is a fact
about the implementation rather than a measurement with variance. They are asserted because the
judge once globbed the same cobertura report twice - coverlet's own and the TRX attachment copy -
and reported 6/6, which every band here waved through because the rate was still 1.0.

personas.name: weak
personas.comment: Calls everything, asserts nothing. Same coverage as the reference, far fewer mutants killed.

personas.name: empty
personas.comment: One trivial test. Must run and score ~0 rather than fail the run.
